To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microwave heating of a wide range of materials can be studied in situ, and that the dielectric properties are a key parameter to understand the behavior of the materials during the heating process.
the dielectric properties of materials are a key to understand and optimize microwave processing.

“the dielectric properties of materials are strongly affected by the temperature and by the microwave power absorbed, leading to different thermal processes, depending on the material and on the process parameters.”
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new methodology based on the in situ characterization and monitoring of microwave-assisted high temperature processes, through the dielectric properties measurements, in order to obtain a better understanding of the interaction between microwave radiation and materials.
the development of microwave-assisted processes in which the dielectric properties of the reacting materials can be used to monitor the reaction progress.
the study and understanding of the dielectric behavior of materials at high temperatures, and the use of this knowledge to develop new materials, processes and technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knowledge of the dielectric properties of the materials involved is a fundamental tool for the design of microwave-assisted processes.
dielectric spectroscopy is a powerful technique for the study of microwave processing at high temperatures.
the in situ measurement of dielectric properties is an effective and powerful tool to study microwave-assisted processes at high temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microwave heating is a powerful tool to modify the structure and properties of materials and to develop new materials.
the dielectric properties of materials are strongly dependent on their composition, structure and temperature.
microwave-assisted processes are very sensitive to the dielectric properties of the materials, which are strongly dependent on the temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric properties of a material can provide information about the microstructure of a material.
dielectric characterization of materials is a powerful tool for in situ monitoring of microwave processing of materials at high temperatures.
dielectric spectroscopy is a very useful technique to characterize materials at high temperatures, and that it is possible to monitor the evolution of the materials’ properties during the process.
